extracted.intended_audience: immigration adjudicators, immigration attorneys, state/local benefit agencies, and public commenters on DHS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from a DHS proposed rule describing which public benefits are counted for public-charge inadmissibility determinations, proposed definitions, exclusions, and factors to be weighed in the totality-of-the-circumstances test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission categories for adopted children (IR-4 / IR-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: IR-4 / IR-9 (Orphan to be adopted by a U.S. citizen). Generally, the parent(s) must complete the adoption in the United States. The child will also be admitted as an IR-4 if the foreign adoption was obtained without either parent having seen the child, or when the parent(s) must establish that they have either 'readopted' the child or obtained recognition of the foreign adoption in the State of residence (this requirement can be waived if there is a statute or precedent decision that clearly shows that the foreign adoption is recognized in the State of residence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These children are generally admitted as lawful permanent residents and USCIS will send a Certificate of Citizenship to the child without a Form N-600 being filed or adjudicated. The discussion contextualizes treatment of adoptive children in relation to citizenship acquisition and the public-charge inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission category for Hague Convention adoptees (IH-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: IH-4 (Hague Convention Adoptee to be adopted by a U.S. citizen). These children are admitted as lawful permanent residents and the parent(s) must complete the adoption in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These children generally will become LPRs and the discussion ties to Child Citizenship Act eligibility and related immigration processing (e.g., N-600K, interview, oath).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa requirement for children eligible to naturalize under section 322
rubrics_metrics.description: Children of U.S. citizens residing outside the United States and eligible to naturalize under section 322 must apply for an immigrant or nonimmigrant visa to enter the U.S. before they naturalize; these children are generally issued a B-2 nonimmigrant visa to complete the naturalization process through interview and taking the Oath of Allegiance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains procedural route for such children and situates their likely interaction with benefit programs and public-charge considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude Medicaid receipt by children of U.S. citizen parents from public-charge consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to exclude from consideration for purposes of the public charge inadmissibility determination receipt of Medicaid benefits by children of U.S. citizen parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: these children will generally become U.S. citizens upon or after admission and families are found to have resources to care for them; excluding such Medicaid receipt is consistent with Congress' interest in supporting U.S. citizens seeking to adopt foreign-born children and is not at odds with PRWORA concerns about incentives for immigration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalization for long-term care at government expense treated as public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to consider institutionalization for long-term care at government expense – at any level of government – as a form of government assistance included in the definition of public benefit. Institutionalization for long-term care is a non-cash, non-monetizable public benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: government-subsidized institutional care satisfies basic living needs (medical care, housing, food) and thus indicates lack of self-sufficiency. Examples include hospital services, ICF/ID, Nursing Facility (NF), PASRR, inpatient psychiatric services for individuals under 21, and services for individuals age 65+ in an Institution for Mental Diseases. DHS would consider parents' or guardians' assets/resources in the totality of the circumstances and would not assume automatic inadmissibility for children or severely disabled persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare generally excluded; include only Part D low-income subsidies as public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS does not propose to consider all of Medicare as part of the definition of public benefits. DHS is only proposing to consider Premium and Cost Sharing Subsidies (i.e., low-income subsidies) for Medicare Part D as part of the definition of public benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Medicare as a whole is not equated with the public benefits targeted by the rule, but the Part D low-income subsidy can impose substantial costs on multiple levels of government and indicates lack of ability to be self-sufficient in satisfying basic medical needs; beneficiaries apply for the Low-Income Subsidy with SSA or State Medicaid agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of subsidized public housing in definition of public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidized public housing and other high-expenditure housing-related benefits are included among designated public benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: public housing provides rental housing for eligible low-income families, elderly, and persons with disabilities; HUD-administered programs use area median income to set eligibility, and such benefits relate to basic living needs and federal/state expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude receipt of public benefits by active duty servicemembers and their families
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to exclude consideration of the receipt of any public benefits by active duty servicemembers, including those in the Ready Reserve, and their families (spouses and children) from public-charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: military service and compensation structures (allowances, tax advantages) may result in reliance on benefits like SNAP without burdening the public; exclusion supports troop readiness and recruitment. Applicants under this exclusion must submit proof of active duty or Ready Reserve service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unenumerated benefits not included in public-charge definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'public charge' would not include receipt of any non-cash public benefit not listed under the proposed 8 CFR 212.21(b). Benefits such as Social Security retirement benefits, general Medicare, and a wide range of Veterans' benefits would not be included; likewise excluded are social insurance programs like workers' compensation and non-cash education and job-training benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states this exclusion supports administrability (e.g., many education benefits are received indirectly through schools). Any exclusively state, local, or tribal public benefit that is not cash assistance for income maintenance, institutionalization for long-term care at government expense, or another specifically listed program would not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective expansion of designated public benefits only in final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any expansion of the list of designated public benefits in a final rule would be prospective in nature (i.e., not effective until following publication of a final rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS invites comments on whether it should expand the list to include specific public benefits that recipients are aware they receive and must opt into, particularly those similar in nature to benefits intended to help low-income people meet basic living needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of CHIP for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS is considering adding the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) to the list of included benefits and requests public comment on whether to include CHIP in a final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: CHIP provides comprehensive health coverage to children in families with incomes above Medicaid thresholds; federal expenditures for CHIP are significant and the program relates to basic living needs (medical care), though participation by noncitizens is currently relatively low. DHS requests comment on inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public benefit receipt by certain alien children (age relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the public charge determination is prospective and considers the totality of circumstances, the age at which an alien child received benefits, and other circumstances of benefit receipt while a child, are relevant considerations in determining whether past or current receipt indicates likely future receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS solicits comment on the best mechanism to administer public-charge determinations for aliens who received benefits while under the age of majority, and whether and to what extent DHS should weigh such past or current receipt as an indicator of likely future receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment on potential modifications by benefit-granting agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS requests public comments regarding how benefit-granting agencies might modify enrollment processes and program documentation in response to a final rule (e.g., advising potential beneficiaries of immigration consequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS seeks information about the time and resources required for such modifications and may use this information to determine an appropriate effective date for a final rule; DHS solicits comments from state, local, and tribal governments and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'likely at any time to become a public charge'
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to define 'likely at any time to become a public charge' to mean likely at any time in the future to receive one or more public benefits, as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b), based on the totality of the alien's circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this proposed definition, DHS would find an alien inadmissible if likely in the future to receive designated public benefits in an amount or for a duration exceeding the proposed thresholds. The definition is prospective and considers totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between current receipt and likelihood of future receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to distinguish between an alien who is a public charge based on current receipt of public benefits and an alien who is likely to become a public charge at any time in the future; current receipt does not automatically render an alien inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving public benefits by itself does not establish that an alien is likely to become a public charge; the statutory test requires an opinion as to the likelihood of future events. Thus, current receipt must be evaluated in context and is not per se disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household size considered in the 'family status' and 'assets, resources, and financial status' factors
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of public-charge inadmissibility determinations, DHS proposes to consider the alien's household size as part of the family status factor, as well as part of the assets, resources, and financial status factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Household size will be one element in the totality-of-the-circumstances evaluation when determining likelihood of future public-benefit receipt.
